deduplication_rule: Related Diagnosis does not imply Duplicate Penalty. The same evidence may support multiple dimensions only when each dimension identifies a distinct structural mechanism; propagated effects must not be presented as independent source defects without evidence.. Do not multiply the same mechanism across multiple dimensions as separate severe penalties unless distinct mechanisms are demonstrated.

D1.name: Level Collapse
questions: At what level(s) of analysis does the work operate?
Are conclusions from one level extended to another?
Has any cross-level transition been explicitly justified?
D1.boundary_note: Cross-level inquiry is legitimate when the transition is argued. Collapse occurs when the transition is silent or unsupported.

anchors.positive: A scientific paper carefully separates empirical findings from philosophical interpretation and states the conditions under which the former may inform the latter.
anchors.negative: Psychological laboratory results are presented as direct proof of a universal moral principle without additional normative argument.
anchors.neutral_or_na: A purely formal mathematical proof that never leaves its own level.

D1.execution_boundary: different levels alone are not collapse

D2.name: Scope Overreach
questions: What range of application does the author claim or imply?
What evidence or argument actually supports that range?
Has the conclusion been extended beyond the conditions that justify it?
D2.boundary_note: Explicit self-limitation of scope is not a defect. Ambition is not overreach; unsupported expansion is.

anchors.positive: A theory of local institutional design states its cultural and historical boundary conditions and refuses universal claims.
anchors.negative: Findings from one demographic sample are presented as universal human nature without further justification.
anchors.neutral_or_na: A narrowly scoped technical lemma that never claims broader application.

D2.execution_boundary: broad claim alone is not overreach; explicit limitation is management

D3.name: Definition Drift
questions: How is the central term first defined?
Does the same term later perform a different conceptual function?
Is any change in meaning acknowledged and justified?
D3.boundary_note: Conceptual development is legitimate when made explicit. Drift is the silent shift.

anchors.positive: An author introduces a technical term, later refines it, and marks the refinement with a clear redefinition.
anchors.negative: A key term begins with one meaning and later silently performs another function while still treated as continuous.
anchors.neutral_or_na: A short argument that uses each key term only once, in a fixed sense.

entry_gate: key term repeats across material inference

D4.name: Observer Ambiguity
questions: From whose standpoint are the principal claims made?
Does that standpoint remain stable?
When the standpoint changes, is the change marked?
D4.boundary_note: Multiple perspectives are valuable; unacknowledged switching is the defect.

anchors.positive: A historical study clearly distinguishes contemporary participant testimony from the historian's retrospective analysis.
anchors.negative: A text moves from first-person lived experience to universal claims about humanity without marking the shift.
anchors.neutral_or_na: A formal logical system with no observational standpoint claims.

D5.name: Temporal Flattening
questions: Does the work treat processes that unfold in time as if they were static states?
Are developmental stages presented as permanent characteristics?
Is temporal structure preserved or compressed out of recognition?
D5.boundary_note: Abstraction is necessary; erasing development is the problem.

anchors.positive: A developmental psychology account carefully limits stage-specific findings to the relevant age range.
anchors.negative: Behaviour observed in a temporary crisis is treated as the permanent character of a people or institution.
anchors.neutral_or_na: A purely synchronic formal model that makes no developmental claims.

D5.execution_boundary: temporal vocabulary or analytic stages alone are not flattening

D6.name: Hidden Premises
questions: Which premises are explicitly stated?
What must be true for the argument to work even though it is not stated?
If the suspected premise is removed, can the argument still proceed?
If an inherited framework is removed, does the system retain its structure?
D6.boundary_note: An explicit premise is not a Hidden Premise. An inherited framework is not a defect merely because it is inherited.

anchors.positive: An author lists the background assumptions of their discipline and states which ones the present argument still requires.
anchors.negative: A conclusion depends on an unstated maximising-rationality premise that carries the weight of the argument.
anchors.neutral_or_na: A fully formalised proof in which every premise appears in the statement of the theorem.

D6.execution_boundary: explicit premise or inherited framework alone is not hidden

D7.name: Category Confusion
questions: What categories are being used?
What conditions make something a member of each category?
Are category boundaries maintained?
Is a property of one category transferred to another without an adequate bridge?
If the categories are separated, does the inference still work?
D7.boundary_note: Similarity in appearance, behaviour, function, or outcome does not by itself establish category identity.

anchors.positive: A philosophy of mind text carefully distinguishes neural correlates from phenomenal experience and refuses to treat them as interchangeable.
anchors.negative: A statistical correlation is treated as if it were a causal mechanism of the same ontological kind.
anchors.neutral_or_na: A taxonomy that never transfers properties across its own categories.

D7.execution_boundary: shared behavior/property alone is not category identity

D8.name: Self-Reference Loops
questions: What premise or framework generates the conclusion?
Is the conclusion later used to validate that same premise or framework?
Is there genuinely independent evidence?
If the return edge is broken, does the justification survive?
D8.boundary_note: Self-reference alone is not a defect. Legitimate self-application is distinct from circular self-validation.

anchors.positive: A methodological framework applies its own criteria to itself, openly records limitations, and remains open to external correction.
anchors.negative: Every criticism of the system is reinterpreted as confirmation that the critic has not yet understood the system.
anchors.neutral_or_na: A linear empirical argument that never refers its conclusions back to its own founding premise.

entry_gate: C returns as support for P
D8.execution_boundary: self-reference/introspection/lack of external testability alone is not loop

D9.name: Context Erasure
questions: What background conditions does the work require?
Does the original argument match those conditions?
Are the conditions preserved as the claim expands or travels?
When context changes, is the change acknowledged?
D9.boundary_note: Concepts may travel; their supporting conditions should travel with them or be consciously reconstructed.

anchors.positive: A legal principle is restated for a new institutional setting, and the author explicitly rebuilds the supporting procedural conditions.
anchors.negative: An ethical rule formulated under specific social assumptions is applied universally while those assumptions are silently dropped.
anchors.neutral_or_na: A purely formal system that claims no empirical or historical context.

D9.execution_boundary: deliberate abstraction or low contextual detail alone is not erasure

D10.name: Language Reification and Infinitization
questions: What is the representation (Rp)?
What is the represented object or reality (Ro)?
Does the work distinguish Rp from Ro?
Does a definition become treated as the totality of the object?
Does a logical or linguistic structure become an ontological structure without an established bridge?
Is a finite, contextual expression treated as if it supplied infinite or universal coverage?
D10.boundary_note: Representation is necessary for thought; the diagnostic issue is an unsupported collapse of representation into represented reality, or of the finite into the infinite.

anchors.positive: A scientific model is repeatedly described as a model, with explicit statements of what it abstracts away.
anchors.negative: A classification scheme is treated as if it were the structure of reality itself, and dissent is treated as denial of reality.
anchors.neutral_or_na: Ordinary technical vocabulary used with clear operational definitions and no ontological inflation.

D11.name: Operational Viability
questions: What practical role does the work itself claim or imply?
What action guidance is actually supplied?
Who must act, coordinate, authorize, fund, maintain, or revise the implementation?
What resources and timescale are required?
What feedback or revision mechanism exists?
What structural barriers stand between the theory and its intended practical role?
D11.boundary_note: A purely theoretical work that does not claim a practical role should not be penalized. D11 may be N/A. Operational Viability is not Practical Desirability.
decision_tree: Does the work claim or clearly imply a practical role? If No → N/A
If Yes → Score against the match between claimed role and supplied operational conditions.

anchors.positive: A policy proposal specifies responsible agents, resource requirements, feedback loops, and known institutional barriers.
anchors.negative: A grand reform program states desirable end-states but supplies no agents, resources, or revision path.
anchors.neutral_or_na: A pure metaphysical system that never claims to guide action.

entry_gate: declared or materially implied practical role

D12.name: Consequence Mapping
questions: What implementation or action is being considered?
Which consequences have actually occurred, and which are only foreseeable?
Who receives benefits, burdens, risks, or responsibilities?
Are consequences reversible or irreversible?
Over what timescales do they unfold?
Are secondary, cumulative, or reflexive effects considered?
Is responsibility for consequences structurally located?
D12.boundary_note: Ordinary causal explanation inside a theory is not the same as consequence mapping of the theory's own practical uptake. D12 may be N/A for purely explanatory works.
decision_tree: Does the work claim or clearly imply practical uptake? If No → N/A
If Yes → Score the completeness and structural differentiation of consequence analysis.

anchors.positive: A technology assessment distinguishes direct effects, distributional effects, irreversible risks, and feedback onto the technology itself.
anchors.negative: A transformative social proposal asserts only intended benefits and treats unintended consequences as outside its concern.
anchors.neutral_or_na: A historical explanation of past events that does not propose present implementation.

D12.execution_boundary: ordinary theoretical implication is not implementation consequence; no implementation => N/A

global_execution_rules.stone_principle: Diagnose what structural condition is present without deciding whether the target ought to be accepted, rejected, preferred, preserved, replaced, or implemented.
global_execution_rules.diagnosis_before_scoring: Evidence -> Structural Identification -> Dimension Classification -> Dependency/Extent -> Severity -> Score.
global_execution_rules.positive_gate: Absence of defect is not positive evidence. Positive scores require active structural management.
global_execution_rules.zero: Evaluated; no significant positive or negative structural condition established.
global_execution_rules.IE: Potentially applicable but evidence is insufficient.
global_execution_rules.dedup: Related Diagnosis != Duplicate Penalty. Reuse evidence only for distinct mechanisms; distinguish source conditions from propagated effects.
